note: Argentine movie-recommendation social site across Latin America; on the 2011-2012 listings, and TNW (Feb 2012) names it among the companies Atomico backed before its first Brazil deals ('the Argentine movie recommendation site Cinemaki'); the round is unnamed and undated on every surface; no press after 2012 - status unknown

Maker of the UberStrike browser shooter (founded Seoul 2007, Beijing team); 'it has just announced that it has raised money from Atomico' (GamesBeat, May 2012) - Atomico was the initial funder, round unnamed and undisclosed; DCM's A-Fund led the next round Feb 2013 (TNW); shut down 2020 (Wikipedia)

Digital entertainment production house (founded 2007 by Michael Wayne and Chris Kimbell; created the Kin Community network in 2011, now the company's name); 'Mayfiled, General Catalyst Partners, and Atomico Investments have put $5 million into Deca.tv' (TechCrunch, Sep 2007; the firm's 2008 page: 'DECA is funded by Mayfield, Atomico, and General Catalyst Partners') - the round is unnamed; still operating as Kin Community (Playa Vista), only its Canadian arm sold to Corus 2019

Synthetic-audience simulation (Alex Cooper, Ben Warner, ex-No 10); 'The total includes a $10 million round led by Atomico' (Tech.eu, Feb 2026; the firm's own post the same day; Ben Blume director from Sep 2025, register) - the round's name conflicts across sources (FinSMEs 'Pre-Seed and Seed', deal counsel 'Series A', no article body names it) -> undetermined

The company behind State (state.com), an opinion network (Alex and Mark Asseily); 'raised $14 million in seed financing in May 2012 from funders such as Atomico' (Wikipedia, citing TechCrunch, which lists 'Niklas Zennstrom of Atomico' but does not name the round - hence medium); on the firm's 2014-2020 listings; inactive by 2020 and Equal Media Ltd dissolved 2024; graduation decided in the S2A pass

Design e-commerce (Jason Goldberg); 'This round serves as Fab's Series C ... was indeed led by London-based VC Atomico Ventures' (TechCrunch, Jul 2012; the firm's own release 'Atomico Leads $105 Million Series C Funding for Fab'); Atomico was not in the a16z-led Series B of Dec 2011; the Fab brand's US assets were sold to PCH International Mar 2015 and the Hem business (Fab's pivot, merged into this row) Feb 2016 -> acquired

Crowdsourced independent-designer fashion (Y Combinator 2010; founders Ari Helgason and Tom Riley); filed under the firm's /portfolios/atomico-ii/ pages 2011-2012; a $400K round of Nov 2010 (Vator headline, page gone) is the likely Atomico round but no fetchable source confirms it -> undetermined; no press after 2012 - status unknown

AI agent for NHS administration (Rachel Finegold, ex-Palantir); 'The London startup announced a $16M seed round led by Atomico ... the first institutional money into the company' (TNW, Jun 2026; Tech.eu gives GBP 9.7M for the round; the firm's own post; Andreas Helbig director of Frontier AI Ltd from Mar 2026, register); censored

Online marketplace/community for mothers (founded 2010, San Francisco); filed under the firm's /portfolios/atomico-ii/ pages 2010-2011; the only round record is a vendor listing (not citable) -> undetermined; no press - status unknown

Free mobile messaging (YC W07, Swedish founders, San Francisco); 'In the summer of 2007 Heysan raised a seed round from Khosla Ventures and Atomico' (YC's company page); on the firm's 2008-2012 listings; acquired by Good Technology May 2009; graduation decided in the S2A pass

Cloud netbook OS, then personal cloud (Tariq Krim); 'has just raised $4.2 million in Series A funding from Atomico Ventures and Mangrove Capital Partners' (TechCrunch, Jul 2009; Zennstrom joined the board); discontinued 2016-04-01 (Wikipedia)

basis: D2 (the founders' own companies, T4): Zennstrom and Friis created Joost in 2006; a founder's company is a member only where an Atomico vehicle held it, and no surface shows one - the only outside round (the $45M of May 2007: Sequoia, Index, CBS, Viacom, Li Ka-shing) had no Atomico, and TechCrunch notes the seed 'presumably ... came directly from them'; the 2008 listing is the founders' history, as with Skype
